references.text: Jesus himself predicts that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected, be killed, and rise on the third day—a direct parallel to the words angels remind the women of in [ref:Luk 9:22|Luke 9:22].

For the third time, Jesus predicts that the Son of Man will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, mistreated, crucified, and rise on the third day ([ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33]). This is one of the central passion predictions that angels refer back to.
Jesus says that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands ([ref:Luk 9:44|Luke 9:44]), which directly corresponds with the expression "handed over into the hands of sinful men" in Luke 24:7.
Also in [ref:Matt 17:22-23|Matthew 17:22-23], Jesus predicts that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, be killed, and rise on the third day—a parallel passion prediction.
In [ref:Matt 20:18-19|Matthew 20:18-19], Jesus predicts that the Son of Man will be handed over, crucified, and rise on the third day, with exactly the same elements mentioned in Luke 24:7.
In [ref:Mark 8:31|Mark 8:31], Jesus begins to teach the disciples that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected, and rise after three days—the first passion prediction in the Gospel of Mark.

In [ref:Mark 9:31|Mark 9:31], Jesus predicts that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands and killed, but will rise after three days. The wording "handed over into human hands" closely corresponds with Luke 24:7.

In [ref:Mark 10:33-34|Mark 10:33-34], Jesus gives the third and most detailed passion prediction in the Gospel of Mark, including betrayal, crucifixion, and resurrection—corresponding to the elements in Luke 24:7.

In [ref:Apg 2:23-24|Acts 2:23-24], Peter proclaims that Jesus, according to God’s deliberate plan, was handed over and crucified by lawless men, but that God raised him up—an apostolic summary of what was predicted in Luke 24:7.

Paul conveys the early confession that Christ died for our sins and was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures ([ref:1 Kor 15:3-4|1 Corinthians 15:3-4]). "The third day" is a central theme linking this to Jesus’ own words in Luke 24:7.

[ref:Hos 6:2|Hosea 6:2] speaks of God making us alive after two days and raising us up on the third day. This Old Testament text has been understood as a prophetic background for the resurrection "on the third day".
